summary: Refusal-risk schedule for a maximum-massing scheme at 115 Vicarage Road, Kings Heath (pre-app 2026/03356/PA). The single decisive constraint is the officer's stated position on scale: a 6m two-storey rear extension WILL be refused as overdevelopment/non-subservience (Design Guide SPD 2022 City Note LW-16, BDP 2017 PG3, DM DPD 2021); 4m two-storey depth with a matching hipped roof is the negotiated ceiling. The 45-Degree Code is currently assessed as PASSED from both neighbours — but only because No.117's conservatory has a solid side wall (code taken from its end, which sits 60cm proud of 115's existing extension) and because No.113's nearest window centre (180cm lateral) exceeds the 136cm existing projection; every additional metre of depth or any change in the datum (e.g. if No.117 rebuilds the conservatory or the officer applies the vertical/elevation test at two-storey height) erodes that headroom. Secondary but real risks: overbearing on No.117 across a 78cm gap at two storeys, roof form (flat roof at two-storey will be resisted — "any roof design should match the existing hipped roof design"), privacy from new first-floor flank windows across the 125cm alley to No.113, and total prohibition on any roof terrace/balcony. Lower-order matters (trees, SuDS/permeable frontage, parking after garage conversion, bin storage, daylight to own deep-plan rooms, garden retention) are each individually survivable with standard evidence but collectively give a refusal-minded officer material. Non-planning flags: Severn Trent build-over agreement, Party Wall Act 1996 notices to both neighbours, and a materially constrained permitted-development fallback (original-dwelling baseline already partly consumed by the 2005 rear extension and the two-storey side extension). Strategy that cannot sensibly be refused: 4m-deep two-storey rear with hipped roof matching the main house, set in from the No.117 boundary at first floor, single-storey element (only) pushed deeper under a separate PD/prior-approval route, obscure-glazed non-opening flank windows, no balcony, with a daylight/45-degree compliance drawing, tree survey, SuDS note and parking statement submitted up front.

facts.topic: Ground 1 — Overdevelopment / lack of subservience (THE decisive ground)
facts.detail: Design Guide SPD 2022 City Note LW-16 (householder additions, LW-16 to LW-22) + BDP 2017 Policy PG3 + NPPF ch.12. The pre-app is explicit and verbatim: the 6m two-storey depth 'would be an overdevelopment... doubling the size of the existing property and would not be subservient' and 'would need to be reduced by 2m to 4m in depth'. This is a pre-stated refusal reason with officer authorship — an application at 6m is near-certain refusal and weak at appeal because the SPD wording ('smaller than the main part of the house and not dominate') is clear. NEUTRALISE: fix two-storey depth at 4.0m exactly as invited; take extra volume in width/single-storey depth instead; annotate a floor-area schedule on the drawings showing extension < original house; quote the pre-app compliance in the Design & Access statement.
facts.value: Risk: HIGH (certain refusal at 6m; low at 4m)

facts.topic: Ground 2 — 45-Degree Code, plan test vs No.117
facts.detail: 45-Degree Code is in Design Guide City Note LW-4 (formerly Extending Your Home SPD / 45-Degree Code SPG), applied via DM DPD amenity policy. Officer currently takes the datum from the END of No.117's conservatory because it has a solid side wall — and that conservatory projects 60cm BEYOND 115's existing extension, gifting extra depth. Fragility: (a) if No.117 demolishes/rebuilds the conservatory with a glazed side or replaces it with a habitable extension, the datum reverts to the original rear windows and the assessment collapses; (b) the concession is officer discretion, not policy right — a different case officer or committee can re-run it from the original openings. Nearest side window is 230cm off the fence. NEUTRALISE: submit a dimensioned 45-degree compliance drawing (plan AND section) taken BOTH from the conservatory end and, as sensitivity, from the original window, showing the 4m scheme passes either way; if it only passes from the conservatory end, keep the deep massing single-storey on that flank.
facts.value: Risk: MEDIUM (currently passes, but on a fragile discretionary datum)

facts.topic: Ground 3 — 45-Degree Code, plan test vs No.113
facts.detail: 115's existing extension already projects 136cm beyond No.113's own rear extension; No.113's nearest window centre is 180cm laterally from 115's extension corner. On plan, a 45-degree line from that window centre tolerates ~180cm of projection beyond No.113's rear building line — so only ~44cm of extra depth on that flank exists before the line is cut. Any 'maximum massing' deepening on the No.113 side beyond ~40cm breaches the code at ground AND first floor. NEUTRALISE: step the plan — full extra depth on the No.117 side (where the conservatory datum gives headroom), chamfer/set-in the No.113 corner, or hold that flank at the existing 3.3m line; show the geometry explicitly on the compliance drawing.
facts.value: Risk: HIGH for any added depth on the No.113 flank; LOW if stepped
facts.source: Measured distances supplied; Design Guide LW-4

facts.topic: Ground 4 — 45-Degree Code, vertical/elevation test and level changes
facts.detail: Birmingham's code guidance (LW-4) allows officers to require MORE than the plan test where scale or level changes worsen shadowing/enclosure — i.e., a vertical 45-degree section from the centre of the nearest habitable window. A two-storey (~5.2-5.7m eaves/wall) mass whose corner sits 180cm from No.113's window centre, and 78cm from No.117's conservatory, will cut a vertical 45-degree line even where the plan line passes. Officers rarely refuse solely on the vertical test for householder schemes but it is available and appeal inspectors use it. NEUTRALISE: hip the roof away from both boundaries (lowers effective height at the flank), keep first-floor flanks set in ~1m from each boundary, and include sections through both neighbour windows in the submission before the officer asks.
facts.value: Risk: MEDIUM (site geometry genuinely tight at two storeys)
facts.source: Design Guide LW-4 caveat text; DM DPD amenity policy

facts.topic: Ground 5 — Overbearing / loss of outlook (BRE 25-degree and enclosure)
facts.detail: DM DPD 2021 amenity policy (development must not cause unacceptable impacts on privacy, daylight, overshadowing, aspect and outlook) + NPPF para on amenity. A two-storey flank wall 78cm from No.117's conservatory and ~3m from her side window would fail a BRE 209 25-degree test taken from that window if the wall faces it, and reads as severe enclosure regardless. Mitigation in the owner's favour: conservatories carry reduced amenity weight, the solid side wall self-screens, and the window centre is 370cm from her rear wall. NEUTRALISE: keep the two-storey element off the shared boundary (single-storey only within ~1m of the No.117 fence), hipped roof pitching away, and commission a short daylight/sunlight note (BRE 209 VSC/25-degree check) from both neighbours' nearest windows — cheap insurance that pre-empts the most common third-party objection.
facts.value: Risk: HIGH if two-storey goes to the No.117 boundary; MEDIUM if set in 1m+

facts.topic: Ground 6 — Overshadowing / loss of daylight-sunlight
facts.detail: Same policy basis as Ground 5. Actual harm depends on orientation, which is not in the brief (open question). If 115's rear faces south/west, the two-storey mass shadows No.113's garden across only a 125cm alley; if north, shadowing falls on 115's own garden and the ground weakens. NEUTRALISE: establish orientation, run the BRE 209 sun-hours-on-ground test for both neighbouring gardens for the 4m scheme, and put the result in the application. If marginal, the hipped roof (mandated anyway) materially reduces the shadow envelope versus flat roof.
facts.value: Risk: MEDIUM (orientation-dependent, unresolved)

facts.topic: Ground 7 — Privacy / overlooking from first-floor windows
facts.detail: DM DPD amenity policy + Design Guide separation-distance guidance. New first-floor REAR windows are generally acceptable (normal back-to-back relationship), but any first-floor SIDE/flank window overlooking No.113 across the 125cm alley or into No.117's garden 78cm away will be resisted unless obscure-glazed and non-opening below 1.7m; oblique views from a deeper rear elevation into No.117's garden may also be raised. NEUTRALISE: no clear-glazed flank windows at first floor (condition-accept obscure glazing), keep principal outlooks rearward, and offer a 1.8m boundary treatment where oblique views arise.
facts.value: Risk: MEDIUM (fully designable-out; certain objection if ignored)

facts.topic: Ground 8 — Roof terrace / balcony / raised platform
facts.detail: Any roof terrace on the flat-roof side extension or on a flat-roofed rear element, or any first-floor balcony, is (a) a near-automatic privacy refusal given 78cm/125cm neighbour gaps, and (b) expressly EXCLUDED from permitted development — GPDO 2015 Sch.2 Part 1 Class A development is not permitted where it includes a veranda, balcony or raised platform (and Class B/C similarly for roof alterations). There is no compliant 'maximum massing' version of a terrace here. NEUTRALISE: omit entirely; if outdoor amenity at level is wanted, a Juliet guard on inward-opening doors (no projecting platform) is the only defensible form and even that invites scrutiny at these separations.
facts.value: Risk: HIGH — treat as prohibited on this site
facts.source: GPDO 2015 SI 596 Sch.2 Pt.1; DM DPD amenity policy

facts.topic: Ground 9 — Roof form / design not matching hipped original
facts.detail: Pre-app verbatim: 'any roof design should match the existing hipped roof design' (LW-16: design must complement the scale and style of the house). Consequences: the existing FLAT-roof two-storey side extension cannot be replicated or extended at two-storey with another flat roof; a mansard, crown-flat, or large box dormers on the hip would conflict; a hip-to-gable conversion changes the 'hipped roof design' the officer has anchored to. NEUTRALISE: hipped roof on every two-storey element, matching pitch/eaves/materials; if loft space is wanted, use rear-facing pitched-roof dormers subordinate in the hip slope rather than a gable conversion, and treat re-roofing the existing side extension with a matching hip as a positive planning-balance card (visual improvement to trade against massing).
facts.value: Risk: HIGH for flat/gabled/mansard forms; LOW if hipped throughout

facts.topic: Ground 10 — Street scene / character and terracing effect (side extensions)
facts.detail: PG3 + LW-16 + DM DPD design policy. The rear massing is largely invisible from Vicarage Road (weakens any street-scene refusal for the rear), but further SIDE widening at two storeys engages Birmingham's long-standing terracing rule: two-storey side extensions should keep a gap to the side boundary (historically ~1m at first floor) and be set back/set down from the main frontage so paired extensions cannot read as a continuous terrace. The house is detached with an existing two-storey side extension, so the front building line and gap are already established — going wider or forward of that line at first floor is the risk. NEUTRALISE: no further sideways first-floor widening beyond the existing flank; keep any side elements behind the front elevation and below the main ridge; state in the D&A that the rear elevation is not visible in the public realm.
facts.value: Risk: LOW for rear massing; MEDIUM if the side extension is widened at first floor
facts.source: BDP 2017 PG3; Design Guide SPD; DM DPD 2021

facts.topic: Ground 11 — Trees
facts.detail: BDP 2017 (TP7 green infrastructure), DM DPD tree/landscape policy, NPPF. No tree information supplied — open question. Mature garden trees within influencing distance of a 6m-deep foundation, or street trees affected by a widened crossover, trigger a BS 5837 survey demand and can found refusal or delay. NEUTRALISE: pre-emptive BS 5837 tree survey + arboricultural impact assessment if ANY tree over ~75mm stem sits within 12m of the works; check the TPO register and Kings Heath conservation-area maps before submission.
facts.value: Risk: LOW-MEDIUM (unknown site facts; cheap to close out)

facts.topic: Ground 12 — Drainage, flooding and permeable surfaces
facts.detail: DM DPD sustainable drainage requirements + BDP TP6 + NPPF ch.14; GPDO Part 1 Class F makes new front-garden hardstanding over 5 sqm permitted ONLY if permeable or draining to a permeable area. A maximum scheme that also paves the frontage for parking (see Ground 13) must show permeable construction. Roof area roughly doubles — soakaway/attenuation note avoids a drainage holding objection. NEUTRALISE: one-page SuDS statement, permeable paving spec on the drawings, rainwater to soakaways sized to BRE 365.
facts.value: Risk: LOW (paperwork ground, but a free refusal reason if omitted)
facts.source: DM DPD 2021; GPDO Sch.2 Pt.1 Class F

facts.topic: Ground 13 — Parking after garage conversion
facts.detail: Birmingham Car Parking Guidelines SPD / DM DPD parking standards. The two-storey side extension sits OVER the garage; a maximum scheme that converts the garage to habitable space removes an off-street space while adding bedrooms (likely 4-5 bed outcome), inviting a highways consultation response. Vicarage Road is a busy B-road in Kings Heath, which cuts both ways (on-street pressure vs sustainable location near the high street and the new Kings Heath rail station). NEUTRALISE: retain two off-street spaces on the frontage drawing (permeable), show cycle storage, and cite the site's sustainable-location credentials.
facts.value: Risk: LOW-MEDIUM (rarely a sole refusal reason for householders)

facts.topic: Ground 14 — Bin storage and frontage clutter
facts.detail: Design Guide SPD expects convenient, screened bin storage that does not dominate the frontage; on a maximum scheme where the side alley is built over, bins can lose their route to the street, which officers now routinely flag. NEUTRALISE: keep or replace a side access route/gate, or show a screened bin store on the front drawing.
facts.value: Risk: LOW (condition-able, not refusal-grade alone)

facts.topic: Ground 15 — Daylight to the OWN dwelling's habitable rooms
facts.detail: NPPF (standards of amenity for existing AND future users) + DM DPD residential standards. A full-width rear addition 4m (two-storey) plus deeper single-storey elements leaves the original rear rooms mid-plan; officers can and do refuse where habitable rooms would rely on borrowed light. NEUTRALISE: open-plan the trapped rooms into the new space, add roof lights over the single-storey element, and label mid-plan spaces as non-habitable (hall/utility) where dark.
facts.value: Risk: LOW-MEDIUM (design-out at plan stage)

facts.topic: Ground 16 — Amenity space / garden retention
facts.detail: DM DPD residential standards (standards for residential development topic area) expect adequate usable private garden retained. A 6m-deep footprint plus patio can push a suburban plot below acceptable retained garden; at 4m this is unlikely to bite for a typical Kings Heath plot but must be evidenced. NEUTRALISE: annotate retained garden area (sqm) on the block plan; keep comfortably above ~70 sqm for a family house.
facts.value: Risk: LOW at 4m depth; MEDIUM at 6m (another reason the 6m dies)

facts.topic: Ground 17 — Permitted development fallback: disqualifiers and baseline erosion
facts.detail: GPDO 2015 Sch.2 Pt.1: (a) BASELINE — 'original dwellinghouse' means as built/as at 1.7.1948; the 2005 rear extension (permitted S/03404/05/FUL, so PD headroom may survive if that was express permission not PD, but cumulative Class A limits count all enlargements) and the two-storey side extension consume Class A tolerance; (b) Class A limits for a DETACHED house: single-storey rear 4m (up to 8m via Larger Home Extension prior approval with neighbour consultation — No.113/No.117 WILL be consulted and objections force an amenity assessment); two-storey rear max 3m depth AND no part within 7m of the rear boundary; within 2m of any boundary eaves max 3m; side extensions single-storey, max half the width of the original house; (c) CONDITIONS — materials of 'similar appearance' to the existing exterior; upper-floor side windows obscure-glazed and non-opening below 1.7m; no veranda/balcony/raised platform; height measured from the HIGHEST adjacent natural ground level (matters if the plot slopes — a flat-roof height claimed from the high side can be unlawful from the low side); (d) check for any Article 4 direction in Kings Heath before relying on PD. NEUTRALISE: get a Lawful Development Certificate (s.192) for whatever PD element is used (e.g. deep single-storey rear via prior approval) BEFORE building, and use the certificated PD scheme as the fallback position in negotiating the planning application.
facts.value: Risk: MEDIUM that assumed PD rights don't exist as imagined — verify before relying
facts.source: GPDO 2015 SI 596 Sch.2 Pt.1 Classes A-H

facts.topic: Ground 18 — Materials
facts.detail: LW-16/PG3 require materials complementing the host; the existing house is presumably brick with a tiled hip, the side extension flat-roofed (likely rendered/felt). Officers will condition matching brick/tile; contrasting cladding on a maximum-massing scheme hands them a design refusal ground on top of scale. NEUTRALISE: matching facing brick and roof tile specified on drawings; accept a materials condition.
facts.value: Risk: LOW (condition-able)

facts.topic: Non-planning flag A — Build over/near public sewer
facts.detail: Not a planning ground but a project-stopper: building within 3m of a public sewer (common along rear garden lines and side alleys — note the 125cm alley to No.113) requires a Severn Trent build-over agreement under the Building Regulations H4 regime; refusal can force redesign of foundations or a piled/bridged solution. NEUTRALISE: obtain the sewer map and, if applicable, the build-over agreement before detailed design.
facts.value: Flag — resolve pre-construction
facts.source: Building Act/Building Regs H4; Severn Trent policy

facts.topic: Non-planning flag B — Party Wall etc. Act 1996
facts.detail: Not a planning ground and NOT a reason for the council to refuse, but with a wall 78cm from No.117's conservatory and works beside a 125cm alley to No.113, s.1 (line of junction), s.2 and s.6 (excavation within 3m and deeper than neighbour foundations) notices to BOTH neighbours are near-certain. Neighbours antagonised by a maximum scheme can slow this via surveyor appointments. NEUTRALISE: serve notices early, budget for two adjoining-owner surveyors, and pair with pre-application neighbour liaison — which also reduces objection letters on the planning file.
facts.value: Flag — programme and neighbour-relations risk

facts.topic: Overall strategy — the scheme that cannot sensibly be refused
facts.detail: (1) Two-storey rear: 4.0m deep (officer's stated ceiling), hipped roof matching the main house, first floor set in ~1m from the No.117 boundary and chamfered/held back on the No.113 corner to clear the 45-degree line from the 180cm window; (2) Single-storey rear: take the extra depth here — up to 6m+ via the planning application (single-storey depth was not the officer's objection) or certificate the 8m Larger Home Extension prior-approval route as a fallback; (3) no balcony/terrace anywhere; obscure non-opening flank glazing; matching materials; (4) submission pack front-loads the evidence: 45-degree plan+section drawing from both datums, BRE 209 daylight note, tree survey or nil-return, SuDS note, parking/bin plan, floor-area subservience schedule, and a D&A that quotes the pre-app back at the officer paragraph by paragraph. The pre-app letter is the roadmap: every quantified concession in it (4m, hipped roof, conservatory-end datum) should be locked into the drawings verbatim so refusal would require the officer to contradict her own written advice.
facts.value: Composite recommendation
facts.source: Synthesis of pre-app 2026/03356/PA and policy set

open_questions: Orientation of the rear elevation (sun path) — determines whether the overshadowing/BRE ground bites on No.113's or No.117's garden or falls away entirely.
Is 115 Vicarage Road within a conservation area or covered by any Article 4 direction (Kings Heath/Moseley fringe)? This would strip or modify the PD fallback and add design scrutiny.

Were the existing two-storey side extension and the 2005 rear extension built under express permission or PD, and what is the exact 'original dwellinghouse' footprint — needed to compute remaining Class A headroom for the Lawful Development Certificate fallback.
Any trees over 75mm stem within ~12m of the works, and any TPOs on or adjacent to the plot.
Location of public sewers relative to the rear and side (125cm alley) — Severn Trent asset map needed before foundation design.
Ground levels: is there any level change between 115 and either neighbour that would trigger the LW-4 'level changes' caveat or affect PD height measurement from highest adjacent ground?

Which specific DM DPD policy numbers apply post-Main Modifications (amenity and residential-standards policies) — verify final adopted numbering against the adopted DPD PDF before citing in the D&A statement.
